aciklama:
A ship floats because of a delicate balance - and the ocean is always trying to break it. Here is why even unsinkable ships go down.

#shorts #engineering #ocean #science #ships

sahneler.metin: A ship floats on a knife edge between buoyancy and gravity.
As long as it pushes away more water than it weighs, it stays up.
But let water inside, and that balance flips in minutes.
Water rushes to one side, the ship tilts, and more water pours in.
This runaway tilt is called loss of stability.
Watertight compartments are meant to stop it, but if they overflow...
...the flooding spreads from room to room until the ship rolls over.
The ocean does not need to be violent, just patient.
Every great ship that sank underestimated the sea.
